title: $\Phi_q$/AJ identification — full AJ statement, significance, and Lean structure
html:
Remark. \Phi_q/AJ identification — full AJ statement, significance, and Lean structure

This note expands prop:phi-q-aj-machinery-identification: the full AJ-conjecture statement, the significance of the unified context-sorting, and the Lean structure of the conditional proposition.

Statement

Let K be a hyperbolic knot complement and J_N(K; q) \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}] its N-colored Jones polynomial. The AJ Conjecture asserts the existence of a non-trivial q-difference operator \hat{A}_K \in \mathcal{A}_q such that:

\hat{A}_K(\hat{L}, \hat{M}; q) \cdot J_N(K; q) \;=\; 0

where \hat{M}f(M) := M\cdot f(M) and \hat{L}f(M) := f(qM), with \hat{L}\hat{M} = q\hat{M}\hat{L}.

The Kashaev-Murakami-Murakami Volume Conjecture for hyperbolic K is governed in the asymptotic by the geometric component of the classical A-polynomial A_K(L, M).

The dilogarithm regulators that appear in the substrate-evaluation chain are exactly:

  • \Phi_q: saddle-point regime of \hat{A}_K \cdot J_N = 0 at q = e^{2\pi i / N} (root-of-unity asymptotic).
  • \mathrm{Li}_2^q: saddle-point regime of \hat{A}_K \cdot J_N = 0 at q \in (0, 1) (real asymptotic, via Stokes).

The two regimes are related by the modular S-transform q \leftrightarrow \tilde{q} = e^{2\pi i / \tau} (conj:modular-s-transform-q-q-tilde).

Significance

The framework previously distinguished \Phi_q vs \mathrm{Li}_2^q contexts pragmatically. Per the AJ identification, both are the same algebraic object (\hat{A}_K) viewed through different archimedean lenses. Wiring this explicitly unifies the context-sorting into a single algebraic statement. It provides the categorical-derivation target for the closure question. The AJ identity holds over \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}]; the framework's Pre-Archimedean / Archimedean split passes through this algebraic gate. The concrete root-of-unity saddle for the figure-eight knot — the \theta = \pi/3 critical point of \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_2(e^{i\theta}), evaluating to \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) — is computed once in the dilog saddle regime.

Lean structure

phi-q-aj-machinery-identification.lean encodes this as a conditional proposition. The backbone is proved unconditionally: the q-Weyl relation, closure of the solution space under linear combinations, and disjointness of the saddle regimes. The conjectural class inputs carry the AJ conjecture's content and the Faddeev/Rogers identifications.

The classes encode literature statements. The framework's contribution is the identification at the algebraic level.

Archimedean specialisation. The \Phi_q / A_J regulator identities are stated over real q with the archimedean ordering 0 < q < 1. This real-analytic regime is the archimedean side of the substrate wall.
